title: Customer Edge Observability Patterns and Decision Log
summary: Working draft that captures recommended patterns for telemetry and audit events emitted from customer-managed networking components in Private deployments, and the decision log for choices we've made so far. This doc is scoped to: connection lifecycle events, operator actions, config-change approvals, keystore/handshake artifacts, and export contracts for customer-facing audit delivery.
goals: 1) Define a minimal, interoperable event model that covers approval gates and forensic needs. 2) Recommend retention and sampling policies that balance customer requirements and Redwood storage costs. 3) Map events to approval/rollback automation to enable faster operator debugging and safe rollouts. 4) Produce a small decision log with rationale to avoid rehashing previous tradeoffs.
assumptions:
- Customers will run a mix of VPC-connected control planes and on-prem edge adapters.
- Not all customers want full 365d retention; offering tiers is necessary.
- We must avoid shipping PII in telemetry; hashes and attestations preferred.
- Approval gates should be automatable via attestation tokens and triage metadata.
requirements:
Functional:
- Emit structured events for: connection_handshake, connection_teardown, config_change_request, config_change_approved, config_change_rejected, keystore_rotation, keystore_access, operator_impersonation_attempt.
- Each event MUST include trace_id and request_id for stitching.
Non-functional:
- Default retention policy should be 90 days for high-fidelity events.
- Tiered retention with ability to export to customer-managed S3 or on-prem archive.
- Streaming export within 2 minutes for audit-critical events.
telemetry_schema:
Canonical field list (CSV): event_type,timestamp_utc,customer_id,site_id,operator_id,actor_type,action,resource_type,resource_id,change_summary,attestation_token,result,latency_ms,bytes_in,bytes_out,trace_id,request_id,hash_redacted_payload.
Notes: customer_id and site_id are stable identifiers; operator_id can be an admin user or operator service principal. attestation_token is the compact signed reference we use in approval flows.
example_event_lines:
Example 1 (connection_handshake): event_type=connection_handshake; timestamp_utc=2025-01-14T21:12:03Z; customer_id=cust-78ab; site_id=eu-west-1-edge-2; resource_id=adapter-a1; actor_type=system; result=success; trace_id=tr-5f2; request_id=req-9c3; hash_redacted_payload=sha256:3b8...
Example 2 (config_change_request): event_type=config_change_request; timestamp_utc=2025-01-20T11:45:12Z; customer_id=cust-78ab; site_id=eu-west-1-edge-2; operator_id=marcus.lee; actor_type=human; change_summary="Bump MTU from 1400->1500"; attestation_token=tok:eyJ...; result=pending; trace_id=tr-7a1; request_id=req-123
retention_policy_recommendation: Tier A (audit-critical): 365 days, all fields, no sampling. Tier B (operational): 90 days, full fidelity but aggregated index for heavy payloads. Tier C (telemetry): 30 days, 1% sampling for verbose debug traces. Export options: daily archives to customer S3 for any tier. Cost justification: combination of sampling + early aggregation reduces active storage by ~45% in simulated workloads.
access_controls_and_privacy:
- All payloads containing potential secrets must be redacted before leaving customer network. Use deterministic hashing (SHA-256) for payload references.
- RBAC: only 'auditor' and 'security' roles can request raw event access; default console view shows redacted/aggregated fields.
- KMS integration: attestation_token signatures must be verifiable with customer-managed keys when requested via Private deployment mode.
approval_gates_instrumentation: Minimum set of events that gate an approval: config_change_request (with change_summary + diffs link), automated_tests_result (pass/fail + coverage), attestation_token (signed by operator or CI), operator_ack (timestamp + operator_id). For high-risk changes we require: automated_tests_result=pass AND operator_ack within 24h AND attestation_token present. Failure paths must emit config_change_rejected with rollback_plan reference.
export_contracts: Supported export sinks: Redwood-managed encrypted S3, customer-managed S3, TLS stream to customer SIEM, syslog-over-TLS to customer aggregator. Format: newline-delimited JSON with canonical fields; provide schema version in metadata header (x-redwood-schema: v1). For compliance customers we will include a signed index file per export day.
observability_patterns:
- Keep key correlation fields (trace_id, request_id) small and immutable across adapters.
- Emit lightweight 'heartbeat' events for adapters every 30s with jitter to detect silent failures.
- Use prefix caching in logs to reduce repeated metadata in bursts (emit metadata only when changed).
- For keystore events, emit both rotation_start and rotation_complete to avoid ambiguity.
decision_log: 2025-01-08: Chose tiered retention (A/B/C) instead of single long retention — reason: cost + customer variability.
2025-01-12: Decided to require attestation_token for high-risk config changes — reason: consistent cryptographic proof for offsite audits.
2025-01-22: Agreed on canonical event field list (see telemetry_schema) to simplify downstream indexing and SIEM ingestion.
migration_and_rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): instrument adapters with minimal events + heartbeat. Phase 2 (4 weeks): enable export contracts and sample retention tiers on a subset of pilot customers. Phase 3 (2 weeks): run chaos tests to validate event continuity and rollback flows. Owners: Phase 1 - Marcus Lee; Phase 2 - Ravi Patel; Phase 3 - Sofia Gomez.
open_questions:
- Do we need HSM-level attestation for extremely regulated customers or is signed tokens adequate?
- Should we provide a guided 'audit bundle' builder in console that packages a days-worth of audit events with verification metadata?
- What SLAs will we commit to for near-real-time export (2min) in Dedicated vs Private deployments?
next_steps: 1) Sync with infra (SRE) to validate heartbeat frequency impacts (owner Marcus). 2) Draft sample NDJSON export and run through SOC checklist (owner Ravi). 3) Schedule pilot with two customers for retention tiers and export (owner Sofia). 4) Add schema v1 to public Confluence page and make PR to telemetry repo for sample parser.
notes_to_self: This doc is intentionally pragmatic — keep iteration cycles short. Expect lots of edge cases around customers with intermittent connectivity; emphasize resumable exports. Link any follow-ups to PD-3421.
references: Confluence: Private Deploy Observability (internal). Jira: PD-3421, PD-3490. PR: private-deploy#256. Slack thread: #private-deploy-ops.
security_considerations: Encrypt exports in transit + at rest. Ensure key rotation events are separately auditable and cannot be bulk-deleted via standard console operations. Consider immutable retention for Tier A under enterprise contracts.
